source.citation: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet ع غ, independent Ayn at 00:03.1–00:04.0 (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023)
source.variation: The page's directly linked ayn.mov demonstrates independent ع in one continuous pen-down run at 00:03.1–00:04.0. From 00:03.1–00:03.5 the pen begins at the upper-right tip, sweeps left, hooks downward, and shapes the open head. Without lifting, it continues from the head at 00:03.5–00:04.0, descends through the left side of the lower bowl, curves around its floor, and finishes toward the right. The adjacent lesson identifies Ayn as a two-way connector and separately prints its contextual shapes. This one-stroke, zero-lift learner path fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh outline while keeping its evidence distinct from the adjacent Ghayn demonstration and its upper dot.

frames.label: sweep left from the upper-right tip and shape the open head
continue down and around the lower bowl without lifting

source.citation: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet ه و ي, independent Waw at 00:45.7–00:46.9 (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023)
source.variation: The page's directly linked waw.mov demonstrates independent و in one continuous pen-down run at 00:45.7–00:46.9. From the lower-right junction at 00:45.7–00:46.5, the pen sweeps left, curves up and around, and closes the small head loop. Without lifting, it continues from the junction at 00:46.5–00:46.9, descends, and curls left through the tail. The adjacent lesson identifies Waw as a one-way connector and gives both consonant w and long-vowel ū values. This one-stroke, zero-lift learner path fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh outline. Arabic و retains its own script-scoped provenance independently of the existing Persian record for the same Unicode glyph and source-backed geometry.

frames.label: sweep left from the lower-right junction and close the small head loop
continue down and left through the tail without lifting

source.citation: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet ي ك ل, independent Yaa at 00:33.2–00:35.0 (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023)
source.variation: The page's directly linked yaa.mov demonstrates independent ي in three pen-down runs. The body begins at the upper right at 00:33.2, descends, turns, and sweeps left through the shallow independent bowl without lifting, finishing at 00:34.4. After one lift, the lower-left dot is placed at 00:34.5–00:34.7. After a second lift, the lower-right dot is placed at 00:34.8–00:35.0. The adjacent lesson identifies Yaa as a two-way connector and separately prints its contextual shapes. This three-stroke, two-lift learner path fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh outline. Arabic ي is U+064A, so its glyph identity and provenance remain separate from Urdu ی (U+06CC), whose independent body has no lower dots and retains its own source-backed order.

frames.label: descend from the upper right into the independent bowl
sweep left through the bowl without lifting
lift, then place the lower-left dot
lift again, then place the lower-right dot

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 一.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–1 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies one ordered stroke for 一. Median 1 runs from the left of the square rightward across the middle, rising very slightly before it settles. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions and pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 上.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 上. Median 1 descends the central vertical from the top toward the base. Median 2 separately starts at the vertical and draws the short middle horizontal left-to-right. Median 3 separately draws the long base horizontal left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all three medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both intervening lifts, and the short-before-long horizontal contrast; Noto's vertical is straighter and both horizontals are flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 个.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 个. Medians 1–2 are exactly 人 — the same left-falling then right-falling pair, from the same peak, that the first writing lesson in this track taught — and median 3 is a single vertical hung beneath the junction. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all three medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions and two intervening lifts; Noto's roof is a little wider than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 么.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 么. Median 1 draws the upper left-falling stroke down-left. Median 2 separately begins at the upper right, falls down-left, turns without lifting near the lower left, and sweeps right along the base. Median 3 separately places the final down-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all three medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving the second stroke's joined turn and two intervening lifts; Noto's first falling stroke is broader and its lower sweep is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

turn and sweep right along the base without lifting
lift, then place the final dot down-right

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 九.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 九. Median 1 falls from the upper right to the lower left across the whole square; median 2 crosses it, bends downward on the right and hooks back at the foot in a single unbroken run. Two strokes for nine, the largest single-digit numeral in the run and among the cheapest to write.

frames.label: draw the long left-falling stroke
lift, cross right, turn downward and hook left at the foot

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 书: two upper folding strokes, the central upright, and the final upper-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order and that the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. The ductus preserves that ordered sequence while fitting its learner pen paths to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline, whose width and proportions differ from the Arphic-derived source graphics.

Median 1 begins at the upper left, runs right and turns downward within the same stroke; median 2 restarts under that turn, descends most of the height of the square, and finishes with a leftward hook. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts both medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the single internal turn, the terminal hook and one intervening lift; Noto's hook is shorter than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 五.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 五. Median 1 is the top bar; median 2 descends from it leaning left; median 3 crosses to the right and turns down; median 4 is the widest stroke and closes the character along the bottom. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions and pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 什.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 什. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 first: a left-falling stroke from the upper centre down-left, then a separately started vertical stroke to the baseline. Median 3 draws 十's horizontal left-to-right, and median 4 separately descends 十's vertical through it. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all four medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving the complete 亻-before-十 component order and three intervening lifts; Noto's left component is narrower and 十's horizontal is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 你.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 你. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 first: a left-falling stroke followed by a separately started vertical. Median 3 restarts at the upper right and falls down-left; median 4 restarts below it, crosses rightward, then hooks down-left without lifting; median 5 restarts at the centre, descends, then hooks left without lifting; medians 6–7 separately draw the lower-left dot down-left and the lower-right dot down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both joined hooks, the component order, and six intervening pen lifts; Noto's right horizontal and hooks are squarer than the source medians, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 儿. Median 1 starts near the upper centre and falls down-left; median 2 restarts at the upper right, descends nearly vertically, bends right along the base, then hooks upward without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those two ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the second stroke's unbroken bend and hook, and one intervening pen lift; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 再.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 再. Median 1 draws the top horizontal left-to-right. Median 2 separately descends the left side. Median 3 restarts at the upper left, crosses the frame's top, turns down the right side, then hooks left at the base without lifting. Median 4 descends the central vertical, median 5 draws the inner horizontal, and median 6 closes with the long bottom horizontal left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both turns inside the enclosing third stroke, the close-last rule, and five intervening lifts; Noto's frame is squarer and its bottom horizontal is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 十: median 1 crosses from left to right, median 2 descends through its centre. Horizontal before vertical, the same order 三 and 四 already used. The character is the lower component of 早 and appeared in this course as a part of that character for thirteen chapters before it was taught on its own.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 口.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 口. Median 1 starts at the upper left and descends the left side; median 2 restarts near the upper left, crosses the top from left to right, turns without lifting, then descends the right side; median 3 restarts at the lower left and closes the bottom from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the joined corner, and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 名. Medians 1–3 draw 夕 first: an upper left-falling stroke, a separately started horizontal that continues down-left without lifting, and a separately placed inner down-right dot. Medians 4–6 then draw 口: the left vertical, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, and the closing bottom horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both joined turns, and five intervening lifts; Noto's 夕 sweep is broader and 口 is squarer than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 吗.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 吗. Medians 1–3 draw the left 口 in the same order the standalone character uses: its left vertical, its joined top and right sides, and its closing bottom horizontal, all inside the upper-left third of the square. Medians 4–6 then draw 马: a horizontal that turns down at the right, a long stroke that turns twice and hooks, and a wide finishing horizontal that runs almost the full width of the character and is the widest stroke in it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, directions, the two joined corners and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

Medians 1–3 draw the left 口 in the same order the standalone character uses and in the same upper-left third of the square that 吗 puts it in. Medians 4–6 draw 尸 — a turning top stroke, a horizontal, and a long left-falling stroke that runs past the bottom of 口 — and medians 7–8 draw 匕 tucked inside it. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the three internal turns and seven intervening lifts; Noto sets 尸's long falling stroke slightly steeper than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 和.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 和. Medians 1–5 draw 禾: the short top left-falling stroke, the horizontal, the long central vertical, then the left-falling and right-falling pair that finish it. Medians 6–8 draw 口 on the right in the same order the standalone character uses. Left component complete before the right one begins. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the joined corner in 口 and seven intervening lifts; Noto compresses 禾's final right-falling stroke into a dot, as the source graphic does, because 口 stands beside it.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 喜.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 喜, and they descend the character in four bands: medians 1–3 the 士 at the top, medians 4–6 a 口, medians 7–8 the short pair beneath it, median 9 the single widest horizontal in the character, and medians 10–12 the closing 口. Top before bottom throughout, and each 口 is built left side, joined top-and-right, closing floor — the order the reader already writes. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all twelve medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the two joined corners and eleven intervening lifts; Noto's ninth stroke runs slightly wider than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 四.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 四. Medians 1–2 build the outer box exactly as 口 does — the left side, then the top and right in one turning stroke; medians 3–4 are the two pieces inside it; median 5 closes the bottom last. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions and pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

and turning up to the right at its foot
lift, then close the bottom with a horizontal héng stroke from left to right

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 国.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 国. Medians 1–2 open the outer frame, medians 3–7 finish every stroke of 玉 inside it, and median 8 closes the frame along the bottom. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians share the coordinate system used for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. The ductus uses those ordered source medians directly; the vendored Noto Sans SC outline can differ in width and proportion from the Arphic-derived source graphics.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 女.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 女. Median 1 starts near the upper centre, makes a short down-right entry, bends down-left to the lower-left junction, then turns without lifting and sweeps down-right to finish; median 2 restarts at the upper right and falls down-left; median 3 restarts at the left edge and crosses the middle from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the first stroke's internal turn, and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 好.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 好. Medians 1–3 draw 女 first: a bent stroke descends down-left and sweeps right without lifting, a separately started stroke falls down-left, and a separately started horizontal crosses left-to-right. Medians 4–6 then draw 子: a horizontal turns down-left without lifting, a separately started vertical descends and hooks left without lifting, and a separately started middle horizontal crosses left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, 女-before-子 component order, all three joined turns, and five intervening pen lifts; Noto's 子 top turn is more angular and its vertical hook is flatter than the source medians, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 子. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both internal turns, and two intervening pen lifts; the Noto base hook is flatter than the source median, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 字. Medians 1–3 draw 宀 first: a down-right top dot, a separately started left-side down-left stroke, and a separately started horizontal roof that hooks down-left without lifting. Medians 4–6 then draw 子: a top horizontal that turns down-left without lifting, a separately started vertical that hooks left without lifting, and a final middle horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all three joined turns, and five intervening lifts; Noto's roof is wider and 子's vertical hook is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 家.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 家. Medians 1–3 complete 宀 from the top dot through the hooked roof; medians 4–10 then complete the lower body from its top horizontal through the central curve, three left-falling strokes, and final right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the roof-before-body order, each unbroken turn, and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

lift, then draw the upper horizontal of the lower body from left to right
lift, then draw its left-falling stroke
lift, then descend the centre and curve to a hook at the base without lifting
lift, then add the short left-falling stroke beside the centre
lift, then add the longer left-falling stroke below it
lift, then add the lower left-falling stroke
lift, then finish with the long right-falling nà stroke

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 对. Medians 1–2 draw 又 as a turning left-falling stroke crossed by a right-falling one; medians 3–5 draw 寸 as a horizontal, a long hooked vertical through it, and a dot placed last. Left component complete before the right one begins, and the dot is the final stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all five medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the internal turn in 又, the terminal hook and four intervening lifts; Noto's 寸 sits slightly higher than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 岁.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 岁. Medians 1–3 draw 山 with its centre vertical first, then the joined left-and-base stroke, then the right vertical — centre before the sides, which is the one place this book's top-to-bottom and left-to-right rules do not decide the order by themselves. Medians 4–6 draw 夕 beneath. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the two internal turns and five intervening lifts; Noto's 山 is wider and flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 我.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 我: an upper-left falling stroke, an upper horizontal, a hooked vertical, a lower rising stroke, a long curved slash that hooks upward on the right without lifting, a separate rising slash up-left, and a final upper-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all seven medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, both joined hooks, and six lifts; Noto's long slash is more curved and its crossing strokes are more geometric than the Arphic-derived source graphics.

frames.label: draw the short upper-left falling stroke
lift, then draw the upper horizontal left to right
lift, then descend the vertical stroke
hook left at the base without lifting
lift, then draw the lower rising stroke
lift, then draw the long curved slash down and right
hook upward on the right without lifting
lift, then draw the separate rising slash up and left
lift, then place the upper-right dot down and right

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 文.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four separately started strokes for 文: the top dot, the horizontal, the long left-falling stroke, and the long right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians share the coordinate system used for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. The ductus uses those ordered source medians directly; the vendored Noto Sans SC outline can differ in width and proportion from the Arphic-derived source graphics.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 日.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 日. Median 1 starts at the upper left and descends the left side; median 2 restarts near the upper left, crosses the top from left to right, turns without lifting, then descends the right side; median 3 restarts at the left edge and crosses the middle from left to right; median 4 restarts at the lower left and closes the bottom from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the joined top-right corner, the inside-before-close order, and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 早.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 早. Medians 1–4 complete 日 first: the left side, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, the middle horizontal, and the separately closing bottom horizontal. Median 5 then draws 十's horizontal left-to-right, and median 6 separately descends its vertical through the horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving the complete 日-before-十 component order, the joined top-right turn, and five intervening lifts; Noto's 日 is squarer and 十's horizontal is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 是.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 是. Medians 1–4 draw 日 first: its left vertical, joined top and right sides, inner horizontal, and closing bottom horizontal. Medians 5–9 then draw a wide horizontal, central vertical, short lower-right horizontal, lower-left falling stroke, and long finishing stroke down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all nine medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, the joined top-right corner, and eight intervening lifts; Noto's lower finishing stroke is broader and flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 有. Medians 1–2 are the horizontal and the long left-falling stroke that cross at the top, in that order — horizontal before left-falling, the rule 大 and 六 already showed. Medians 3–6 build 月 beneath: left side, then the joined top-and-right that hooks at the base, then the two inner horizontals, so the enclosure is closed before it is filled. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the joined corner, the base hook and five intervening lifts; Noto's 月 is slightly narrower than the source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 看. Medians 1–4 form the upper hand-like element; medians 5–9 complete 目 below. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order and that the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. The ductus preserves that ordered sequence while fitting its learner pen paths to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline, whose width and proportions differ from the Arphic-derived source graphics.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 见.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 见. Median 1 descends the frame's left side. Median 2 separately draws the top horizontal and turns down the right side without lifting. Median 3 draws the inner left-falling leg. Median 4 separately descends the second leg, bends right along the base, and finishes with an upward hook without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all four medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the frame-before-legs sequence, all three joined turns across the top-right frame and vertical-bend hook, and three intervening lifts; Noto's upper frame is squarer and its hooked leg is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 讠.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 讠. Median 1 starts at the upper left and draws the dot down-right; median 2 restarts at the left edge, rises slightly across the short horizontal, turns without lifting to descend, then turns again without lifting and finishes up-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those two ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both turns inside the second stroke, and one intervening pen lift; Noto's middle horizontal and descent are squarer than the source median, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 请.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 请. Medians 1–2 draw 讠: a down-right dot, then a separately started short horizontal that turns down and finishes up-right without lifting. Medians 3–10 draw 青: two upper horizontals, a central vertical, a wide middle horizontal, the lower left side, a separately started lower top horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks left at the base without lifting, then two inner horizontals. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all ten medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all four internal turns across 讠 and 青, and nine intervening lifts; Noto's 青 horizontals are flatter and its lower enclosure is squarer than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 谢. Medians 1–2 draw 讠: a down-right dot, then a separately started short horizontal that turns down and finishes up-right without lifting. Medians 3–9 draw 身: an upper falling stroke, the left side, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks left at the base without lifting, two inner horizontals, a wide lower horizontal, and a lower falling stroke down-left. Medians 10–12 draw 寸: a horizontal, a separately started vertical that hooks left at the base without lifting, and a final down-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all twelve medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all five internal turns across 讠, 身, and 寸, and eleven intervening lifts; Noto's 身 enclosure is squarer and 寸's hook is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

In the 00:50–00:55 lowercase а demonstration, the rounded body and right-hand finishing stem are written in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated handwritten а is a round single-storey form; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a double-storey printed form with an extra upper shoulder. This learner path preserves the source's one-run body-to-stem motion while fitting that shoulder as the entry into the lower loop. Connected cursive may add entry and exit joins, and individual handwriting may round or slant the body differently.

source.variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 01:54–01:57 lowercase г demonstration, the pen rises from the baseline into the main shoulder, descends and turns at the baseline, then continues through a smaller rising-and-falling exit arch in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand is a rounded cursive form with two humps; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a block-like printed form with one straight upright and a top bar, and has no exit arch. This learner path preserves the source's baseline-to-shoulder-to-baseline lift count while fitting the printed form: climb the upright, sweep right along the top bar, reverse to the junction, and descend the upright without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's smaller exit arch, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, or slant both humps differently.

In the 07:50–07:55 lowercase у demonstration, the pen begins at the upper left, descends to the baseline, turns upward without lifting through the right arm, retraces down through that arm into a long descender, curls left around a lower loop, crosses the descender, and rises into a short rightward exit in one continuous pen-down run, for zero intervening lifts. The demonstrated school hand resembles a loop-descender Latin y with a narrow rounded upper body and rising exit; the bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a printed y-like form with two straight upper arms and a broad descender that curves left without a loop or exit join. This learner path preserves the source's left-arm-to-right-arm-to-descender order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: descend the left arm, rise through the right arm, retrace to the junction, continue through the long descender, and curve left through its terminal without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's lower loop and rising exit, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, widen, or slant the upper body and descender differently.

source.variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 08:42–08:49 lowercase х demonstration, the pen begins at the upper left, curves right and descends through the middle crossing, sweeps left into a lower terminal, then lifts once. The second run begins at the upper right, curves left and descends through the same crossing, then sweeps right into a small rising exit. The demonstrated school hand therefore uses two facing curved runs with one intervening lift: a right-bulging left stroke followed by a left-bulging right stroke. The bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a printed X-like form with four straight diagonal arms meeting at the centre and no entry or exit joins. This learner path preserves the source's upper-left-run-before-upper-right-run order, top-to-bottom directions, crossing, and one-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: trace the two straight left arms through the centre, lift, then trace the two straight right arms through the same centre. Connected cursive restores the source's facing curves and rising exit, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, widen, or slant the curves differently.

source.variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 09:24–09:28 lowercase ч demonstration, the pen begins at the upper left, descends the short left stem to a middle join, turns through a narrow rounded bridge, rises to the top of the right stem, descends that full stem to the baseline, and curls into a small rising exit without lifting. The demonstrated school hand therefore uses one continuous pen-down run with zero intervening lifts: short left stem down, joined rise, long right stem down, then the curled exit. The bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a printed ч-like form with a shorter straight left stem, a shallow rounded bowl, and a full-height straight right stem, without the narrow bridge, curled baseline, or exit join. This learner path preserves the source's short-stem-to-bowl-to-long-stem order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: descend the short left stem, sweep through the shallow bowl, rise along the right stem, and descend the full right stem without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's narrower bridge, curled baseline, and rising exit, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, widen, or slant the bowl and stems differently.

source.variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 10:45–10:56 lowercase ы demonstration, the pen begins near the upper left, curls through a narrow entry loop, descends the tall left stem to the baseline, turns right, circles the joined lower bowl counterclockwise, and closes it against the stem. The pen then lifts once, restarts at the upper right, descends the separate tall right stem, and curls into a small rising exit. The demonstrated school hand therefore uses two pen-down runs with one intervening lift: the left stem and lower bowl first, then the separate right stem. The bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a printed ы-like form with a straight full-height left upright joined to a wide closed lower bowl and a separate straight full-height right stem, without the narrow entry loop or curled exit. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-right-stem order, within-body counterclockwise direction, and one-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: descend the left stem, circle and close the lower bowl, lift once, then descend the separate right stem. Connected cursive restores the source's narrow entry loop and rising exit, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, widen, or slant the stems and bowl differently.

source.citation: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase ю demonstration, 11:44–11:58, YouTube, 5 February 2013
source.variation: The native-teacher video presents all 33 Russian letters first in print and then in the classic handwritten form taught at school. In the 11:44–11:58 lowercase ю demonstration, the pen curls through a small looped entry, descends the tall left stem to the baseline, turns through a rising diagonal connector, and continues directly into the right oval. It rises around the oval's upper-left side, sweeps across the top, descends the right side, rounds the bottom, and rises along the left side to close without lifting. The demonstrated school hand therefore uses one continuous pen-down run with zero intervening lifts: left stem down, joined connector, then the clockwise right oval. The bundled Noto Sans Cyrillic glyph is a printed ю-like form with a straight full-height left upright, a horizontal middle bar, and a wide closed oval, rather than the source's looped entry, diagonal connector, and narrow cursive oval. This learner path preserves the source's stem-to-connector-to-oval order, clockwise oval direction, and zero-lift evidence while fitting the printed outline: descend the left stem, retrace to the middle and cross the bar, then circle the right oval clockwise and close it without lifting. Connected cursive restores the source's looped entry and diagonal join, and individual handwriting may round, narrow, widen, or slant the stem, connector, and oval differently.

source.variation: The four buildup frames show four ordered pen-down runs: frame 1 starts at the upper-left and carries the upper curve into the lower bowl without lifting; frame 2 restarts at the middle junction and sweeps right through the shoulder; frame 3 descends the right stem top-to-bottom; frame 4 draws the shirorekhā left-to-right, for three intervening lifts. Thomas Egenes, Learning the Sanskrit Alphabet, p. 12 (Maharishi International University Press, 1990), documents a six-stroke traditional Sanskrit form instead. This learner path follows the four-run modern form and fits its joins and directions to Noto Sans Devanagari.

source.variation: The 27-frame animation shows three ordered pen-down runs over its gray guide: frames 2–19 start at the upper spiral's inner-right tip, curl clockwise around the small opening and outward to the left waist, then continue down and clockwise around the broad lower bowl to the right-stem junction without lifting; frames 20–22 restart at the right stem's headline junction and descend top-to-bottom; frames 23–25 restart at the headline's left edge and draw the shirorekhā left-to-right, for two intervening lifts. The 250 ms holds at frames 19 and 22 mark the first two run endings before the one-second completed frame 26. This learner path follows that sourced three-run order and fits its joined spiral-and-bowl body to Noto Sans Devanagari; everyday handwriting may narrow, divide, or simplify the loops differently.

source.variation: The 15-frame animation shows three ordered pen-down runs: frames 0–9 start at the upper loop's lower inner tip, sweep left and clockwise around the upper loop, descend the joined trunk, curl clockwise around the lower bowl, and continue right through the crossbar without lifting; frames 10–12 restart at the right stem's headline junction and descend top-to-bottom; frames 13–14 restart at the headline's left edge and draw the shirorekhā left-to-right, for two intervening lifts. The spatial restarts at frames 10 and 13 delimit the three runs; all frames last 100 ms, so this source provides no long inter-stroke holds. The Central Hindi Directorate's 2019 Deskbook on Orthography of Devanagari Script, Lesson 2, Unit VII, p. 38, independently confirms the upper loop and trunk, lower bowl and crossbar, right stem, and headline order, while staging the upper and lower body parts separately rather than proving their join. This learner path takes its three-run lift count from the animation and fits its curves to Noto Sans Devanagari; everyday handwriting may divide or simplify the joined body differently.

source.variation: The 22-frame animation shows four ordered pen-down runs over its gray guide: frames 2–5 start beneath the headline, curve clockwise around the inner curl, and finish at the left waist; frames 6–13 restart at that waist, curve down and right around the lower bowl, and rise to the right-stem junction; frames 14–16 restart at the right stem's headline junction and descend top-to-bottom; frames 17–20 restart at the headline's left edge and draw the shirorekhā left-to-right, for three intervening lifts. The 190 ms hold at frame 5 and 250 ms holds at frames 13 and 16 mark the first three run endings before the one-second completed frame 21. The Central Hindi Directorate's 2019 Deskbook on Orthography of Devanagari Script, Lesson 2, Unit VIII, p. 41, independently shows the same inner curl, lower bowl, right stem, and headline buildup and directions. JackPotte's 11-frame ‘Devanagari j य.gif’ animation of 29 March 2009 instead joins the inner curl and lower bowl before the same separately descended right stem and left-to-right headline. This learner path follows the mutually corroborated four-run form and fits its curves to Noto Sans Devanagari; everyday handwriting may use the documented three-run join or simplify the bowls differently.

source.variation: The 23-frame animation shows four ordered pen-down runs over its gray guide: frames 2–9 start at the open lower-left tip, curve up and clockwise around the left loop, and finish at the inner junction; frames 10–12 restart at that junction and sweep the diagonal arm up-right to the right stem; frames 13–17 restart at the right stem's headline junction and descend top-to-bottom; frames 18–21 restart at the headline's left edge and draw the shirorekhā left-to-right, for three intervening lifts. The 250 ms holds at frames 9, 12, and 17 mark the first three run endings before the one-second completed frame 22. The Central Hindi Directorate's 2019 Deskbook on Orthography of Devanagari Script, Lesson 2, Unit VIII, p. 43, independently shows the same left loop, diagonal arm, right stem, and headline buildup and directions. JackPotte's 12-frame ‘Devanagari l ल.gif’ animation of 29 March 2009 instead draws the right stem first in frames 0–2, then the diagonal arm in frames 3–5, the left loop in frames 6–8, and the headline in frames 9–10; all frames last 100 ms, so it provides no long inter-stroke holds. This learner path follows the mutually corroborated loop-first four-run form and fits its loop and arm to Noto Sans Devanagari; everyday handwriting may use the documented stem-first order or simplify the loop differently.

source.variation: The published data names letter ळ and contains three ordered path arrays. Stroke 1 has 128 points: it starts at the center junction, sweeps left around the complete left loop and back through the center, then continues right around the complete right loop and returns to the center without lifting. Stroke 2 has 10 points at one x-position and descends from the headline area to the top of the right loop. Stroke 3 has 36 points and advances from the headline's left edge to its right edge, for two intervening lifts. The companion Devanagari Alphabet page describes the control as a stroke-by-stroke visualization and renders its guide in Martel Sans. This learner path preserves the source's three-array order while fitting the joined figure-eight body to the bundled Noto Sans Devanagari outline; other handwriting may narrow, tilt, or join the upper stem differently.

source.variation: The 13-frame animation shows four ordered pen-down runs: frames 0–4 start just below the headline, descend the left stem, curve left around the central hook, and continue diagonally down-right through the tail without lifting; frames 5–6 restart at the central junction and draw the middle crossbar left-to-right; frames 7–9 restart at the right stem's headline junction and descend top-to-bottom; frames 10–12 restart at the headline's left edge and draw the shirorekhā left-to-right, for three intervening lifts. The spatial restarts at frames 5, 7, and 10 delimit the four runs; all frames last 100 ms, so this source provides no long inter-stroke holds. The Central Hindi Directorate's 2019 Deskbook on Orthography of Devanagari Script, Lesson 2, Unit IX, p. 47, independently shows the same left curve, diagonal tail, middle crossbar, right stem, and headline order, but stages the left curve and tail separately rather than proving their join. The four-run lift count therefore comes from the animation. This learner path follows that animation-backed form and fits its hook and tail to Noto Sans Devanagari; everyday handwriting may divide or simplify the joined body differently.

source.variation: The 22-frame animation shows three ordered pen-down runs over a gray guide. Frames 2–12 start at the right stem's headline junction, descend top-to-bottom, sweep left through the shoulder, and curve clockwise around the hooked body to its lower-right tip without lifting. Frames 13–16 restart at the body's left junction, sweep down-left around the outer curve, and continue diagonally down-right through the tail. Frames 17–21 restart at the headline's left edge and draw the shirorekhā left-to-right, for two intervening lifts. A 230 ms hold at frame 12 and a 250 ms hold at frame 16 delimit the first two runs before the one-second completed frame 21. The Central Hindi Directorate's 2019 Deskbook on Orthography of Devanagari Script, Lesson 2, Unit IX, p. 48, independently shows the same right stem, leftward shoulder, hooked body, outer curve and tail, then headline buildup, but stages the joined first body across more component steps. The three-run lift count therefore comes from the animation. This learner path follows that animation-backed form and fits its turns and directions to Noto Sans Devanagari; everyday handwriting may divide or simplify the body differently.

source.variation: The teaching app animates અ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper-left tip, sweeps clockwise around the open left curve, continues through the broad lower body, rises into the middle shoulder, and finishes through the small right arch. The animation then lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate right stem before curving into the lower-right foot. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph has the same open left curve, joined lower body, middle shoulder, small right arch, and separate full-height right stem, but its printed proportions are broader and its joins more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-right-stem order and one-lift evidence while fitting those movements to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, or slant either run differently.
